audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. All-points height inequality fails for a mixed isotrivial map; Invalid finite-map pull-push inference in central equidistribution lemma; Unequal-degree exceptional maps invalidate universal commensurability
limitations: All-points height inequality fails for a mixed isotrivial map — Counterevidence: Both curve projections dominant; no finite base shrink repairs counterexample. Isotrivial-free1.11 unaffected.

Invalid finite-map pull-push inference in central equidistribution lemma — Counterevidence: Counterexample concerns general finite-map reasoning, not all dynamical hypotheses; lemma and main theorem not counterexampled.
Unequal-degree exceptional maps invalidate universal commensurability — Counterevidence: Theorem1.10 requires equaldegree and is not refuted; arithmetic dependency trace retained.
Nonconstant conjugacies may keep diagonal constant — Counterevidence: No theorem1.3 counterexample; nonweak-special example checked.
Limitations: Publisher-final PDF not acquired; no journal-final equality inferred from author versions.
Limitations: Local replacement does not reprove external Yuan–Zhang, Ax, Julia-symmetry, Manin–Mumford or height-coincidence theorems.
Limitations: No author-code reproduction was required or executed.
Limitations: Remaining corrected unequal-degree theorem and intended expanded special locus require explicit author formulation.

1 — Counterevidence: This is not a counterexample to the isotrivial-free Theorem1.11. The defective extension uses geometric height-zero implies preperiodic in a coordinate where that implication is false. The example refutes the asserted all-points extension, while the downstream proof needs only generic small sequences.

2 — Counterevidence: The example refutes a general inference; it does not satisfy all dynamical/small-sequence hypotheses of Lemma5.2 and does not refute that lemma or the main relative conclusion. The required symmetry of the actual limiting measure can instead be proved.

3 — Counterevidence: Theorem1.10 imposes equal degrees, and the later test-function application uses that equal-degree result. This example therefore does not invalidate the principal equal-degree chain.
4 — Counterevidence: This is not a counterexample to Theorem1.3. Simultaneous conjugacy identifies the common-preperiodic intersection with one fixed pair and leaves its cardinality unchanged.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.
The report retains counterevidence and unresolved questions. Publication does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific adjudication remains pending; author adoption has not been requested.
